title: BazarDor — Bangladeshi Market Price Platform
subtitle: A Bangla-first way to follow the daily prices of everyday essentials.
description: A Bangla-language web platform for exploring daily market prices in Bangladesh, with category browsing, price sorting, comparisons across time periods and market-wise price ranges.
coverAlt: Illustration of a rising price chart beside a price tag. Placeholder artwork, not a screenshot of BazarDor.

facts.label: Interface language
facts.value: Bangla, with Bengali text and numerals

overview: BazarDor is a Bangla-language web platform for exploring daily market prices in Bangladesh. It organizes essential products such as rice, lentils, cooking oil, vegetables, fish, meat, eggs, dairy products and spices.
The interface uses Bengali text and numerals and presents changes in essential commodity prices in an accessible format.
problem: Following changes in the prices of essential commodities, across products, time periods and markets, is easier when the numbers are organized in one place and shown in the language people use every day.
goals: Make daily market prices easy to browse by category.
Show how prices have moved and where they differ between markets.
Keep the experience Bangla-first, including numerals.
features: Category browsing across essentials: rice, lentils, cooking oil, vegetables, fish, meat, eggs, dairy products and spices
Price comparisons across different time periods
Bangla-first interface with Bengali text and numerals

architecture.summary: A Next.js application written in TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS and daisyUI, with authentication through Better Auth backed by MongoDB, deployed on Vercel.

layers.title: Interface
layers.description: Next.js and React pages, styled with Tailwind CSS and daisyUI.

layers.title: Price data
layers.description: Market prices are retrieved from an external source and transformed into the shapes the interface needs.

layers.title: Accounts
layers.description: Authentication with Better Auth, using MongoDB.

challengesNote: These are the areas this project touches, not a first-hand account. A fuller write-up is still to come.
challenges: Depending on an external price API whose availability and shape can change
Transforming raw market-price data into consistent, comparable displays
Building reusable page structures across many product categories
Adding authentication to a data-heavy interface
Keeping price formats and Bengali numerals consistent everywhere

title: Gatekeeper — Logic Puzzle and Story Game
subtitle: A retro 2D story game where the puzzles are built from logic gates.
description: A retro-inspired 2D story and puzzle game that combines dialogue choices, original pixel-art environments and an interactive circuit-building puzzle system.
coverAlt: Pixel-art illustration of an XOR logic gate with input and output wires. Placeholder artwork, not a gameplay screenshot.
overview: Gatekeeper is a retro-inspired 2D story and puzzle game combining dialogue choices, original environments, pixel-art presentation and an interactive circuit-building puzzle system.
Players work with logic gates including NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR and IMPLY, constructed from fundamental logic components.
goals: Connect software development, digital logic, game design and interactive problem-solving in one project.
features: Logic gates including NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR and IMPLY, built from fundamental logic components

architecture.summary: A Java 17 project built with Gradle and rendered with Java 2D.

layers.title: Narrative
layers.description: Dialogue choices set in original environments.

layers.title: Puzzle system
layers.description: An interactive circuit builder where gates are assembled from fundamental logic components.

challengesNote: These are the areas this project touches, not a first-hand account. A fuller write-up is still to come.
challenges: Making a circuit-building puzzle that stays faithful to digital-logic rules
Balancing story pacing against puzzle difficulty
Keeping dialogue branches manageable as they grow

title: XOR Gaming Cafe & Restaurant Management System
subtitle: A console-based C++ system for running a café and a gaming zone.
description: A console-based restaurant and gaming-zone management system in C++ using object-oriented programming and file handling: menu, inventory, kitchen queue, game rentals and a central register.
coverAlt: Illustration of a game controller and a coffee cup beside an XOR symbol. Placeholder artwork, not a screenshot of the program.
overview: A console-based Restaurant and Gaming Zone Management System written in C++ using object-oriented programming and file handling.
The system simulates the operations of a gaming café: food service, inventory management, kitchen workflow, game rentals and financial register management.

featureGroups.title: Authentication and roles
items: Login, sign up and forgot password
Role-based access for Admin, Chef and Customer

featureGroups.title: Food menu
items: Add, update and delete food items
Food names, prices, recipes, ingredients and ingredient quantities
Menu data persisted in binary files
Food availability shown based on inventory

featureGroups.title: Inventory and orders
items: Add ingredients and refill or update stock
Customers place food orders, validated against ingredient availability
Ingredients deducted automatically after valid orders
Orders blocked when required ingredients are unavailable
Simulated transaction loading screen using chrono

featureGroups.title: Kitchen workflow
items: Valid orders are pushed into the kitchen queue
Chefs view pending orders and the recipes for ordered food

featureGroups.title: Game catalogue and rentals
items: Admins add or remove games with name, genre, description and release date
PlayStation 1 to 4 rentals with one to four controllers
Customers choose rental durations and time slots; fully booked slots are shown as unavailable
Admins can change prices and available slot counts
Two controllers: 150 BDT per hour or 100 BDT per 30 minutes
Each additional controller: +50 BDT per hour or +30 BDT per 30 minutes

featureGroups.title: Register and transactions
items: One register for food purchases, game rentals and cash-outs
Tracks total cash, best-selling food item, most-rented game and total income from café and game zone
Transactions stored in files with timestamps

architecture.summary: A modular C++ codebase. Each responsibility lives in its own header and source pair, with role-specific front-ends sitting on shared domain modules and file-based storage.

layers.title: Role interfaces
layers.description: What each kind of user can do.

layers.title: Register and storage
layers.description: Central financial record plus persistence in text and binary files.

notes: Each module is a .h and .cpp pair, except main.cpp.
Uses STL containers including vector, queue and map, and chrono for simulated loading screens.

challengesNote: These are the areas this project touches, not a first-hand account. A fuller write-up is still to come.
challenges: Keeping file-based persistence consistent across modules
Validating and deducting ingredients correctly when orders are placed
Tracking time-slot availability for game rentals
Keeping one register accurate across the restaurant and the gaming zone
Enforcing role-based access for Admin, Chef and Customer
futureImprovements: Unit tests for inventory and rental rules
liveNote: This is a console application that runs locally, so there is no browser-based demo.
runLocally: Compile the sources with GCC, or open the project in Code::Blocks, after obtaining the repository and the required source files.
